summary.short: Section 29A of the UK Copyright, Designs and Patents Act 1988, in force from 1 June 2014, lets a person with lawful access copy a work for non-commercial computational analysis research without infringing copyright, subject to acknowledgement and transfer limits; contract terms blocking such copying are unenforceable.
summary.long: Section 29A, inserted by the Copyright and Rights in Performances (Research, Education, Libraries and Archives) Regulations 2014 with effect from 1 June 2014, is a text and data analysis exception. Under subsection (1), copying a work by a person with lawful access does not infringe copyright if the copy is made so that a person with lawful access can carry out computational analysis of anything recorded in the work for the sole purpose of non-commercial research, and the copy is accompanied by a sufficient acknowledgement unless that is impossible for reasons of practicality or otherwise. Subsection (2) makes copyright infringed if the copy is transferred to another person without the copyright owner's authorisation, or is used for any other purpose without authorisation. Subsection (3) treats a dealt-with copy as an infringing copy for that dealing and, if that dealing infringes, for all later purposes. Subsection (4) defines dealt with as sold or let for hire, or offered or exposed for sale or hire. Subsection (5) makes unenforceable any contract term that purports to prevent or restrict copying that the section permits. The provided text sets no penalties; the section operates within the Act's general copyright infringement rules.
